record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Do there exist achievable Cantorvals whose boundaries have positive Lebesgue measure?

evidence.quote: Do there exist achievable Cantorvals with boundaries of positive Lebesgue measure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n < \infty$. The achievement set (or set of subsums) of $(a_n)$ is defined by
$$E(a_n) := \Bigl\{ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n a_n : (\varepsilon_n) \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Bigr\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}.$$
It is known that $E(a_n)$ is always a nonempty compact set, and that it is one of the following: a finite union of closed intervals, a set homeomorphic to the Cantor ternary set, or a so-called Cantorval. A Cantorval (more precisely, an $\mathcal{M}$-Cantorval) is a nonempty compact subset $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that $C$ is the closure of its interior, both endpoints of every connected component of $C$ are accumulation points of one-point components of $C$, and $C$ has no isolated points. A Cantorval $C$ is called achievable if there exists a summable sequence $(a_n)$ of positive reals such that $C = E(a_n)$.

The boundary $\partial C$ of a Cantorval $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is taken with respect to the standard topology on $\mathbb{R}$, and $\lambda$ denotes Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Does there exist an achievable Cantorval $C$ such that $\lambda(\partial C) > 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open in general. Recent work (Nowakowski–Prus-Wiśniowski, 2025) introduced a family of "standard" achievable Cantorvals and proved that every standard achievable Cantorval has boundary of Lebesgue measure zero; this family includes all known examples (multigeometric Cantorvals such as Guthrie–Nymann, Ferens, Guthrie–Nymann–Jones, as well as several non-multigeometric ones like the Kyiv and Marchwicki–Miska Cantorvals). However, whether every achievable Cantorval is standard is itself open, so the existence of an achievable Cantorval with boundary of positive Lebesgue measure remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Lebesgue measure of boundaries of multigeometric Cantorvals
status_evidence.snippet: All standard achievable Cantorvals have boundaries of Lebesgue measure zero; this family contains all known multigeometric and many non-multigeometric examples.
status_evidence.claim: All currently known achievable Cantorvals have boundaries of Lebesgue measure zero, but the general question is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open problem whether there exist achievable Cantorvals whose boundaries have positive Lebesgue measure.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a recent survey of achievement sets.
